title: Twin Pregnancy: Timing and Mode of Birth

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman with a twin pregnancy planning birth: timing by chorionicity, antenatal corticosteroids and mode of birth, using NICE NG137.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG137 as extracted gives no corticosteroid dose or regimen.
Intrapartum management of the second twin was not captured.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Planned birth is offered at 37 weeks for dichorionic diamniotic twins and at 36 weeks for monochorionic diamniotic twins, after considering antenatal corticosteroids. Continuing dichorionic twins beyond 37+6 weeks, or monochorionic twins beyond 36+6 weeks, increases the risk of fetal death. Monochorionic monoamniotic twins are born between 32+0 and 33+6 weeks, by caesarean section. After 32 weeks vaginal or caesarean birth are both options if the first twin is cephalic with no contraindications or significant size discordance.

clinicalManagement.title: Plan timing
actions: Dichorionic diamniotic: 37 weeks; monochorionic diamniotic: 36 weeks; monoamniotic: 32+0 to 33+6 weeks.

clinicalManagement.title: Consider corticosteroids
actions: Do not give routine steroid courses; consider before planned preterm birth.

clinicalManagement.title: Choose mode of birth
actions: Cephalic first twin and uncomplicated: vaginal birth or caesarean section after 32 weeks; otherwise caesarean section.

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG137 advises against routine corticosteroid courses and to consider them before planned preterm birth, with no dose given. Follow the local obstetric protocol and product information.
